title: Read and write cron time fields
summary: cron runs a command on a schedule. Each scheduled job is one line in your crontab: five time fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) followed by the command, or a shortcut such as @daily.

что значат пять звёздочек в crontab

steps.explain: Check that the crontab tool exists. If nothing is printed, cron is not installed: on Debian, Ubuntu and Mint install the cron package, on Fedora and Arch install cronie. macOS has crontab built in.
Show the jobs already scheduled for your user. This only reads the table. On a new account it prints 'no crontab for <USER>' and exits with status 1; that is normal.
steps.expect: Your existing job lines, or 'no crontab for <USER>' if you have none yet.

steps.explain: Read the time fields in the manual. Look for the list 'minute 0-59', 'hour 0-23', 'day of month 1-31', 'month 1-12' and 'day of week 0-7' with its note that 0 and 7 are both Sunday. The output is long; the first line says CRONTAB(5).
steps.expect: A long text whose first line starts with 'CRONTAB(5)', containing the field ranges listed above.

steps.explain: Each job is one line: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week, then the command. '*' means any value. Example: '30 2 * * *' runs at 02:30 every day.
Inside a field you can use a list such as 1,15, a range such as 1-5 (inclusive), or a step such as */5. So '*/5 * * * *' runs every 5 minutes, and '0 9 * * 1-5' runs at 09:00 Monday to Friday.
Month and day of week also accept names: jan, feb ... and mon, tue ... (case does not matter). Sunday is 0 or 7 in the day of week field, or sun.
Shortcuts replace the five fields: @reboot runs the command once when the machine starts. Example line: '@daily echo hello', which runs once a day.

Add or change jobs with crontab -e, which opens your editor on your table. Add one line per job, save and quit; the table is installed when you save. Lines that start with # are comments and are ignored.

verify.expect: Your job lines exactly as you typed them, for example '30 2 * * * echo hello'.

warnings: cron runs jobs with a short PATH and no terminal: use full paths such as /usr/bin/python3 in a job, and send its output to a file.
A percent sign % in a crontab command means newline, so write it as \% (the manual explains this).
crontab -r removes your whole table without asking. Run crontab -l first and look at what you would lose.

A job that is due while the computer is asleep may be skipped. For macOS, launchd is the built-in scheduler for your own jobs: plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents loaded with launchctl. cron also works on macOS.
